newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - May 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - NZ Business weeklies - May 23.

text.p: Equiticorp costs $100k each day: The Crown's appeal against the $328 million judgment arising from the controversial sale of its New Zealand Steel stake to Equiticorp will be the longest in Appeal Court history. Page 1.

Treasury paper says taxes must rise 26pc over 50 years to sustain superannuation: Governments will have to raise taxes 26 percent over the next 50 years to support the current system of superannuation, a confidential 1997 Treasury report says. Page 3.

New acting SFO chief: Retired district court judge Ronald Jamieson has been appointed acting director of the Serious Fraud Office to allow the interim acting director, David Bradshaw, to return to the State Services Commission. Page 3.
Fire service hot for Card callout system: The New Zealand Fire Service is considering joining the controversial Card emergency call out system. Page 6.

Blue Star Line moves its HQ to Auckland: After 60 years based in Wellington, the Blue Star Line has joined the exodus of shipping companies from the capital and established its head-quarters in Auckland. Page 7.

Analysts remain optimistic despite Telecom's slow growth problems: While the company described last week's profit result as "disappointing", the market remains optimistic about its ability to grow profits. Page 10.

Trade Ministers sets off in pursuit of a dream: International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith is advocating a new wide-ranging free-trade agreement between the countries of the Americas and Asia to speed up the Apec liberalisation process. Page 11.

Multinationals unhappy with IRD's transfer pricing ideas: Inland Revenue faces legal challenges by powerful multinationals if it tries to implement some transfer pricing measures, a UK expert has warned. Page 11.

Hormone dispute may see New Zealand suffer the bull rush: The New Zealand export meat industry is analysing potential implications of a World Trade Organisation ruling that a European Union ban on imports of hormone-treated beef from the US is illegal. Page 13.

Coalition agreement hamstrings Mercury's plans for Power NZ: The shotgun wedding ending the Power New Zealand takeover battle has tipped successful suitor, Mercury Energy, into another minefield -- government policy on electricity ownership. Page 1.

Fishing Bill bungle goes to select committee: The Fisheries Ministry continued billing fishermen for over-fishing their quota, even when it knew the fishermen weren't overfishing at all, a Parliamentary select committee was told on Thursday. Page 3.

Saatchis, Network win referendum account: Advertising agency Saatchi & Saatchi and public relations firm Network Communications have won the $4.75 million job of informing the public about the referendum on compulsory superannuation. Page 6.
